apis.name: YouTube API
apis.tagline: Transcripts, metadata, comments, channels, playlists and search for any public YouTube video.

endpoints.description: The transcript of a video as timed segments and plain text. Without `lang` you get the video's default caption track. format=vtt puts a WebVTT subtitle file in `text`; format=chunks returns `chunks` (index, text, start, end in seconds) with the chunk_size and chunk_overlap used: whole segments merged into pieces of about chunk_size characters, ready for embeddings.

params.name: lang
params.description: Language code (e.g. `en`, `it`, `pt-BR`); auto-translated when the video doesn't have it

params.name: format
params.description: `json` (segments + text), `text` or `srt`. `vtt` (WebVTT subtitles in `text`) or `chunks` (timestamped chunks for embeddings, in `chunks`).

params.name: chunk_size
params.description: `format=chunks` only: target characters per chunk (segments are never split)

params.name: chunk_overlap
params.description: `format=chunks` only: characters of whole segments repeated from the end of the previous chunk (less than `chunk_size`)

endpoints.description: The caption tracks available for a video, manual and auto-generated.
Title, description, channel, duration, views, likes, comment count, tags and categories.
The chapters of a video with start and end times in seconds.

Top-level comments of a video with author, likes, replies count, date and pinned flag. With include_replies=true each comment also carries `replies` (comment_id, parent_id, text, author, like_count, published_at), up to replies_per_comment each. Replies are billed like comments: 1 credit per 100 comments and replies together.

params.name: include_replies
params.description: Also return each comment's replies, in its `replies` list (billed like comments)

endpoints.description: Channel details by channel ID (`UC...`) or @handle.
The videos of a channel, newest first, page by page: follow `pagination.next_cursor`; every page costs the same, the last one like the first.

The videos of a public playlist in playlist order, page by page: follow `pagination.next_cursor`; every page costs the same, the last one like the first. `meta.total_videos` and `meta.total_pages` give the size of the playlist (null when YouTube does not show it). Private and Mix playlists answer 404.

params.name: playlist_id
params.description: Playlist ID: the `list=` value of a playlist URL (`PL...`, `UU...`, `OLAK5uy_...`)

endpoints.description: Search by keyword and get videos with channel, duration, views and upload date.

apis.name: Meta Ad Library API
apis.tagline: Search the ads running on Facebook and Instagram, with creatives, dates and advertiser.

endpoints.description: Ads matching a keyword or an advertiser page, with filters, up to 30 per call. Every ad carries days_active (whole days from started_at to ended_at, or to today while it runs; null when unknown) and winning_score (0-100, null when days_active is null): long-running ads are the ones that pay off. score = L + V + R, with L = 70 x min(days_active, 90) / 90, V = 15 x min(variants_count - 1, 9) / 9 and R = 15 x min(log10(1 + EU reach) / 6, 1). The EU reach is only in the single-ad lookup, so in lists score = (L + V) x 100 / 85: a missing reach never lowers it. Rounded to the nearest integer. min_days_active and sort=longevity apply to the ads of the returned page, at the same price.

params.name: page_id
params.description: Only ads of this advertiser page

params.name: sort
params.description: Order. `longevity` puts the longest-running ads of the page first.

params.name: min_days_active
params.description: Keep only ads running for at least this many days (applied to the returned page, same price)

params.name: limit
params.description: Ads per page (max 30, one page of the source)

endpoints.description: One ad with creatives, payer and beneficiary, and EU/UK transparency data.

params.name: country
params.description: Country used to look the ad up

endpoints.description: Advertiser pages whose ads match a keyword.

params.name: limit
params.description: Pages (max 10, one page of the source)

endpoints.description: Advertiser page details with Instagram account and active ads estimate.
The ads of one advertiser page, with the same filters as search. Every ad carries days_active and winning_score (see Search ads for the formula); min_days_active and sort=longevity work as in search.

params.name: sort
params.description: Order. `longevity` puts the longest-running ads of the page first.

params.name: min_days_active
params.description: Keep only ads running for at least this many days (applied to the returned page, same price)

params.name: limit
params.description: Ads per page (max 30, one page of the source)
